title: [VSC-0] Breakdown: audit moe-vscode against JetBrains, decide plugin reuse, slice this epic
definitionOfDone: docs/plans/2026-11-02-vscode-reuse.md exists with four sections: the baseline (snapshot sha, plus the result of moe-vscode `npm ci && npm test && npm run compile`), the JetBrains → VS Code gap list, the reuse decision with reasons, and a slice table naming every created task id.

The epic holds the slice rows, created with moe.create_task. Each has a mechanically checkable DoD and names its files. The first wave of at least two rows has pairwise-disjoint files and no unmet dependencies.
No slice row plans any file from the description's list of files to avoid (the wrapper lane, WT docs, role docs and initFiles.ts).
Exactly one final integration-and-hardening row exists, and it depends on every other slice row.
This row's own diff changes only docs/plans/2026-11-02-vscode-reuse.md, plus board records.

implementationPlan.description: Baseline, then create the doc with its `## Baseline` section. Run nothing with npm in the shared checkout (GLOBAL rail). Snapshot recipe (mem:gotcha-vscode-gate-from-wsl): S=/mnt/d/moe-scratch/vsc0-$(git rev-parse --short HEAD). The absolute path must contain NO UUID-shaped segment: npm 12 redacts UUIDs in `npm list` output (prints `***`), vsce then collects zero files and `npm run package` fails with "Extension entrypoint(s) missing" (the architect hit this on 2026-11-02 with the snapshot in a Claude scratchpad path; write this finding into the doc). Run `mkdir -p $S && git archive HEAD | tar -x -C $S` from the repo root and record the full `git rev-parse HEAD`. Let E='env -i HOME=$HOME PATH=$HOME/.nvm/versions/node/v24.21.0/bin:/usr/local/bin:/usr/bin:/bin'. (a) In $S/moe-vscode run the DoD command `$E bash -c 'npm ci --no-audit --no-fund && npm test && npm run compile'`, recording its exit code and the node:test summary (tests, pass, fail, skipped), then `$E npm run lint`. (b) Packaging: `$E bash -c 'npm ci --no-audit --no-fund && npm run build'` in $S/packages/moe-daemon and in $S/packages/moe-proxy, then `$E npm run package` in $S/moe-vscode. Unzip the .vsix into $S/vsix and, from the repo root, run `node scripts/tests/onboarding.mjs $S/vsix/extension/bundled`; record the vsix file count and size. Error handling: a failing command is a finding, not a reason to stop or retry blindly. Record its exact command, exit code and last 20 output lines in the doc; a later command that depends on it is marked not run, with the reason. If a test file that a peer's wip checkpoint put on HEAD is red, follow mem:gotcha-snapshot-gate-peer-wip-checkpoint and record both runs. Delete $S afterwards, even after a failure. Create docs/plans/2026-11-02-vscode-reuse.md with: an H1 title; a short intro (epic epic-aabc654d; the human's goal verbatim, "Make sure our VSCODE is working and we reuse as much as we can between plugins"; date 2026-11-02; written by VSC-0, task-a3e414a3dce848e6939081e5cbf941ce); then `## Baseline` with the 40-hex sha, every command with its exit code and counts, the packaging result, the UUID-path finding, and, for comparison, the architect's pre-epic run at 882a4c39f618e61ca6159c360e236e88dd925ee4 (lint 0; compile 0; 388 tests, 384 pass, 4 skip (Windows-only), 0 fail; package OK with 4105 files and 61.37 MB using --no-dependencies, an equivalent file set because .vscodeignore drops node_modules/**; onboarding PASS). Add a `### Daemon wire` subsection. Re-derive the lists yourself with `grep -o -E "sendMessage\('[A-Z_]+'" moe-vscode/src/services/MoeDaemonClient.ts | sort -u` (plus CLIENT_HELLO and READINESS_REQUEST = GET_EXECUTION_READINESS), `grep -o -E "case '[A-Z_]+'" moe-vscode/src/services/MoeDaemonClient.ts | sort -u`, `grep -o -E '"[A-Z_]{4,}"' moe-jetbrains/src/main/kotlin/com/moe/services/MoeCommandSender.kt moe-jetbrains/src/main/kotlin/com/moe/services/MoeMessageDispatcher.kt`, `grep -n "case '" packages/moe-daemon/src/server/WebSocketServer.ts` and the StateChangeEvent union in packages/moe-daemon/src/state/StateManager.ts. The architect found: JetBrains also sends RELEASE_TASK, DEREGISTER_WORKER and the five account commands (ADD_ACCOUNT, REMOVE_ACCOUNT, MOVE_ACCOUNT, RENAME_ACCOUNT, SET_ACCOUNT_SWITCH_PERCENT); JetBrains also handles CHANNEL_DELETED, WORKER_DEREGISTERED and PROPOSAL_DELETED (the daemon never emits PROPOSAL_DELETED); VS Code drops ACCOUNTS_UPDATED and ACCOUNT_ADDED on purpose; neither client handles PINS_UPDATED or RESOURCE_UPDATED (chatStore.ts and resourceStore.ts emit them); both speak CLIENT_HELLO and the plan-approval wire with expectedPlanRevision. Verdict to state: VS Code speaks the current wire for everything it implements, and the gaps are missing features, not wire breaks.

implementationPlan.description: Write `## Gap list (JetBrains → VS Code)` and `## Reuse decision`. Gap list, as a table with columns: what JetBrains has (cite the file), VS Code at baseline, row(s). G1: task-status notifications (MoeMessageDispatcher's TASK_UPDATED/TASK_CREATED branch notifies via MoeNotificationService on AWAITING_APPROVAL, BLOCKED, REVIEW and DONE); VS Code has none; VSC-1. G2: <root>/.worktrees excluded from indexing (util/WorktreeExclusion.kt); VS Code's watcher and search crawl every worktree; VSC-2. G3: Delivery section in task detail (toolwindow/DeliveryPresentation.kt); VS Code has no type and renders nothing; VSC-3, VSC-8. G4: one blocker presentation (toolwindow/TaskBlockerPresentation.kt); VS Code keeps two copies (src/panels/TaskDetailPanel.ts and media/board.js) and no test pins their parity; VSC-4, VSC-9. G5: settings edits approvalMode, speedModeDelayMs, agentCommand and enableAgentTeams, and shows the effective landing policy read-only (MoeSettingsDialog.effectivePolicyRows); VS Code lacks enableAgentTeams and the policy, and still edits autoCreateBranch, branchPattern and commitPattern, which no launcher reads; VSC-5, VSC-10. G6: Release Agent (RELEASE_TASK) in task detail and on the card; VS Code has none; VSC-6, VSC-11. G7: CHANNEL_DELETED removes the channel; VS Code ignores it, so the dead channel stays; VSC-6. G8: Accounts tab (rotation list; add, sign in, remove, move, rename, switch percent; five senders); VS Code drops ACCOUNTS_UPDATED and has no UI; VSC-7, VSC-12 to VSC-15. G9: AgentSeatTracker deregisters a seat whose terminal closed (DEREGISTER_WORKER with terminal_closed, acknowledged by WORKER_DEREGISTERED); in VS Code a closed terminal's worker keeps its tasks; VSC-19, VSC-20, VSC-21. G10: build.gradle.kts bundles every docs/roles file, while bundle-assets.mjs bundles 3 role docs, and the two lists are kept by hand; VSC-16. G11: CI packages and smoke-tests the JetBrains zip on PRs, but the vsix is packaged only at release, and packaging after `npm run compile` ships stale dist/ tsc output plus eslint.config.mjs; VSC-17. Then a 'Not sliced' list with reasons. D1 "Run Agents in WSL" toggle: VS Code Remote-WSL runs the extension host inside the distro, so it becomes a manual check in VSC-18. D2 project selector / MoeProjectRegistry: VS Code binds a window to workspaceFolders[0]; deferred until asked. D3 stop the spawned daemon when the last project closes (registry refcount): needs a human decision, because agent seats share the supervised daemon. D4 live Activity Log tab: moe.showActivityLog opens a log document; accepted difference. D5 explicit Initialize Moe action: VS Code runs the daemon's `init` on connect when .moe is missing; accepted. D6 keyboard shortcuts: low value, deferred. D7 PINS_UPDATED and RESOURCE_UPDATED: neither client handles them; a JetBrains-first follow-up. D8 the bundled node_modules ship devDependencies (vitest, typescript, rolldown) in both plugins: a VSC-16 follow-up. Notes: JetBrains' notifyConnectionLost/notifyConnectionRestored are never called; role docs and skills need no VS Code sync, because the daemon rewrites .moe/roles and .moe/skills at every start (packages/moe-daemon/src/index.ts writeInitFiles/writeSkillFiles). Reuse decision, listing every option with its verdict and reason. O1 host VS Code's webviews in JetBrains via JCEF: maximum reuse, but it rewrites the primary IDE's UI, JCEF is missing in some JetBrains setups, and the epic forbids regressing JetBrains; rejected. O2 shared TypeScript client-core package: only VS Code can consume TypeScript; rejected. Type-importing packages/moe-daemon/src/types/schema.ts into VS Code was also considered: tsconfig rootDir is src, so it changes the emit layout and couples compiles to schema churn; deferred. O3 compute presentation in the daemon and serve it on /ws: a true single source, but it changes the wire and docs/SCHEMA.md and docs/MCP_SERVER.md, which are frozen for this epic; deferred. O4 client-neutral golden corpora, CHOSEN: extend CQ-I06b's moe-jetbrains/src/test/resources/client-verdicts.json (27 approval and 23 VM rows today). One JSON file per shared behaviour (client-delivery, client-blocker, client-settings-policy, client-accounts, client-seat-tracker), executed by a Kotlin test and a moe-vscode test. JetBrains writes it first. A disagreement is fixed or filed, never given a client-specific expectation, and consumer rows never edit it. O5 shared strings at test time, CHOSEN: VS Code labels for corpus keys must equal MoeBundle.properties; a generated build-time catalog is deferred. O6 shared bundle manifest, CHOSEN: scripts/bundle-manifest.json (VSC-16). O7 shared launcher, KEPT: both plugins already launch seats through the bundled scripts/moe-agent.{ps1,sh}. Criterion: use a corpus when the logic branches or renders text in both clients; a four-status rule like VSC-1's notifications is ported with mirrored tests.
implementationPlan.note: Gap list (G1-G11), Not sliced (D1-D8) and Reuse decision (O1-O7) written; cited files spot-checked with ls. Other dirty paths are peers'; untouched.
